title: Tile a 2xN Corridor
statement:
A secure corridor consists of a grid of `2` rows and `N` columns of storage cells. Every cell must be covered by exactly one partition. The approved partition modules are:

- A **vertical partition** covering a `2 × 1` block (both rows of one column).
- A **square partition** covering a `2 × 2` block.
- An **L-shaped partition** covering three cells of a `2 × 2` block, which may be installed in any of its four rotations.

Partitions must lie completely inside the corridor and must not overlap. A horizontal `1 × 2` piece is **not** available. Two configurations are different if some cell is covered by pieces of different shapes or positions.

Count the number of valid ways to cover the whole corridor. Since the answer can be very large, print it modulo `10^9 + 7`.
inputFormat: A single integer `N`, the length of the corridor.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of valid configurations modulo `10^9 + 7`.

examples.explanation: The 2 × 2 corridor can be filled by two vertical partitions or by one square partition. Three cells of an L piece leave one cell that nothing can fill.

Three vertical pieces; a vertical piece followed by a square; a square followed by a vertical piece; and two ways of fitting two L pieces together to fill the 2 × 3 block (the two interlocking L pieces can be placed in two mirrored ways).

Looking at the last column: ending with a vertical piece leaves a 2 × 3 corridor (5 ways); ending with a square leaves a 2 × 2 corridor (2 ways); ending with an L that sticks into column 3 (two orientations) forces a second L to complete it and leaves a 2 × 1 corridor (1 way each). Total 5 + 2 + 2 = 9.

hints: Let f(n) be the number of ways to fill a 2 × n corridor. Look at how the last column can be covered.
If the last column holds a vertical piece you are left with f(n-1); a square leaves f(n-2). Think about which L placements are even possible at the end, and what shape remains after you place one.

A single L leaves a single uncovered cell that nothing but another L can fill, so L pieces always arrive in interlocking pairs covering a 2 × 3 block. This gives f(n) = f(n-1) + f(n-2) + 2·f(n-3), computed iteratively modulo 10^9 + 7.
